transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, it's probably not a huge deal, just a little communication hiccup I've been having. I'm a jeweler, and lately, when people ask me a really simple question at the shop—like, um, just asking when a ring repair will be ready—my answer sort of... gets away from me? 

Like, I'll start out talking about the invoices, but then somehow I'm talking about garden soil, and then suddenly I'm on about mortgage papers. And I can just see the poor customer looking at me, and I know they're completely losing me. It’s a little embarrassing, honestly, because I always want to give them a good experience. 

Is... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you? I hope I'm making sense.
Have you been sleeping less than usual without feeling tired?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. Honestly, if I don't get a full night's sleep, I definitely feel it the next day. Working with tiny stones and clasps at the bench takes a lot of focus, you know? So I try to be really good about keeping a regular bedtime. 

I definitely get tired if I miss out on my sleep, just like anyone else, I suppose. Did... did I answer that okay? I hope that's what you were asking.
Has your tendency to jump from one topic to another been present for most of your life?

Oh, no, no, not my whole life at all! I've always prided myself on being very organized and clear-headed. It's just... well, it started maybe a little less than two years ago? 

Right around the time my husband and I took out the business mortgage for the shop. It was a stressful time, of course, taking on that kind of commitment, so I'm sure it's just a little stress reaction, you know? Just a temporary thing that's hung on a bit longer than I'd like. 

It's really just been since then. Does that... does that timeline make sense to you? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?.

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I have so much to be grateful for, you know? The shop is doing okay, and my husband is so supportive. 

But... lately, or I guess for a while now, there have been these stretches. Like, most mornings I wake up with this... this flat, heavy sadness. It's almost like the color has just drained out of the house before I even get up to go to the shop. It's probably just normal fatigue, right? Everyone gets a little down sometimes. 

It does tend to stick around for a few weeks at a time, but I really try to just push through it and put on a smile for the customers. I hope it doesn't make me sound ungrateful to admit that. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?
Have there been times when you were not feeling depressed but your speech still jumped from topic to topic like this?

Um... well, yes, I suppose there was a time like that. I really hope it doesn't sound too strange, but... before I started feeling so heavy and sad, I was actually doing quite well. I was still running my jewelry-making classes and keeping up with the gardening at home. 

But during that time, for maybe a few weeks... I did have this... well, I guess my thoughts were a bit scattered then, too. I kept thinking I was hearing these noises coming from the polishing room when no one was in there. And I got really worried that the customers were somehow watching the business, like, keeping tabs on us? 

It sounds silly now, saying it out loud, and I'm sure it was just my imagination running away with me from being so busy. But I wasn't feeling depressed then at all. I was just... a little overly concerned, maybe? Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.
How long did these unusual experiences continue while you were not feeling depressed?

Well, um, I'd say it was for several weeks. Like I mentioned, it was right before that heavy, sad feeling really settled in. I was still doing all my normal things, you know, running the classes and keeping up with my garden. 

But for those few weeks, I just kept hearing those noises from the polishing room and... and having those worries about the customers watching us. I really hope I'm explaining this right. I know it probably sounds a bit odd, but it was just for that little stretch of time. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
During those weeks of feeling sad, did you lose interest or pleasure in activities you would normally enjoy?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful, because I really am so lucky to have my shop and my students. 

But... I suppose during those heavy weeks, things just don't sparkle the way they usually do. I used to absolutely love hunting for old, vintage clasps at estate sales, and planning out these little jewelry-making classes for the beginners. It was my favorite part of the week. 

But lately... or, during those sad stretches, I just kind of... I find myself mostly staring at the trays of beads and findings, and I just feel like... like none of it is really worth starting. It's awful to admit that, because I know I should be enthusiastic for my students. I really do try to force myself to care, I promise. Do you think that's just because I'm tired, or... is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you heard noises in the polishing room or felt customers were watching the business, did you firmly believe those experiences were real even when there was no clear evidence or others disagreed?

Um... well... I don't want you to think I'm being unreasonable or anything. I try really hard to be practical. But... yes, I suppose I did feel pretty certain about it at the time. 

I know it probably sounds a bit odd, but... I've gotten so convinced that some of the customers are coming in just to check whether I'll miss payments on the shop. They just ask so many questions about the new showroom, you know? And... well, my husband tells me I'm overthinking it, that they're only being friendly and making conversation. And I'm sure he means well, and maybe he's right to try and calm me down. 

But in those moments, it just feels so real to me. I just can't shake the feeling that they have some other motive. I really hope that doesn't make me sound paranoid or difficult. I try not to let it show when they're in the store. Is it okay that I felt that way? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you ever had a sustained period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable compared with your usual self?

Um... elevated or irritable? No, I don't think so. I really try to keep an even keel, especially at the shop. I mean, I know I get sad sometimes, like we talked about, but I've never had a time where I felt... unusually high-energy or angry for days on end. 

I always want to make sure I'm pleasant with the customers and my students, so I really do my best to keep my temper in check. I don't think I've ever had a period like what you're describing. Does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer.
During those periods of sadness and loss of interest, how much did they interfere with your ability to work or manage your usual daily activities?

Well, um... I really do try my best to keep everything running smoothly. I don't want to let anyone down, especially my clients. But... I suppose during those sad times, things do slip a little bit. 

I've, um... I've actually had to cut back on taking custom work lately. It's just... I hate admitting this, but I've been missing some of my repair deadlines. And when I'm sitting down with a client for a consultation, I just sort of... lose track of what we're talking about. My mind just wanders, no matter how hard I try to focus on them. 

And, um, my husband has had to start double-checking all the invoices for me. I used to do all of that myself, without any problems at all. I feel terrible putting that extra work on him. I really am trying to get back to normal, I promise. Do you think it's okay that I need a little extra help right now? I just hope I'm not doing a terrible job at everything.
During the periods when you felt depressed and lost interest, were you also hearing noises or believing that customers were watching or monitoring your business?

Um... yes, I suppose they were happening together. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I know everyone has hard times, but... yes. 

During those worst months, when I was feeling so incredibly heavy and sad, and just couldn't find the energy for the shop... that was also when I was hearing my name in the polishing room. And it was exactly then that I felt so certain the customers were coming in to check up on our payments. 

I really tried to keep it all separate, and I did my best to put on a brave face for everyone, but... it all just sort of hit me at once. I'm sorry if that's a lot to lay on you. Is it normal for those things to happen at the same time? I just hope I'm explaining it in a way that makes sense to you.
Was there a continuous period of at least two weeks when you heard or believed these things, while you were not depressed at all?

Well, um... yes, actually. I don't want you to think I was completely falling apart the whole time, because I wasn't. There was a stretch, um, right before the sadness really took over... I was still doing okay. I was running my jewelry classes, and I even kept up with my gardening, which I love. 

But during that time—I think it was for a few weeks—I was already hearing those noises from the polishing room. And... I was already worrying so much that the customers were watching the business. I really tried to just push through and act normal, you know? I hope it's okay that I didn't mention that right away. I just didn't want to sound like I was complaining too much. Does that help answer your question?
